passages.provision_quote: Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex.
passages.note: Enacted text of the single-subject bill prints the operative provision; it names no voter, so actor and tally are null here.
Bill overview lists Bolick as a co-sponsor of SB1165, among the House members who also appear on the House Third Reading roll call.

rows.reasoning: Bolick co-sponsored and voted Yes on SB1165 (2022), a single-subject Arizona bill whose operative section designates school athletic teams by biological sex and provides that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" "may not be open to students of the male sex". That matches the rung requiring transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth, and the bill's own section C, which does not restrict eligibility for "males", "men" or "boys" or "coed" or "mixed" teams, excludes a complete ban from any organized sports competition. The 31-24 House tally is not near-unanimous, and the act falls in her House term in this same legislature.
